steps.title: What this room is
steps.text: The organization is the boundary. Control Hub is the console where users, roles, locations, services, and devices are made real. Every later room assumes this map.

steps.title: Takeaway 1
steps.text: Control Hub is the single dashboard Cisco documents for managing users, permissions, calling, meetings, messaging, and devices. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 2
steps.text: The first sign-in can start a setup wizard; accepting terms creates the organization, and the activation email address is the sign-in identity used to set the administrator password. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 3
steps.text: People you add start with no administrative privileges. A full administrator assigns prebuilt roles, and can also assign roles to groups. [cite:2]

steps.title: The admin mental model
steps.text: Cisco’s own overview calls Control Hub the central interface to manage the organization, users, services, and usage analytics, and says the first screen is an overview of services that are active or available. [cite:5] Treat that sentence as the product boundary: if a task is “change how Webex works for this customer,” the documented front door is this console, signed in at https://admin.webex.com when you are…

steps.title: What this room is
steps.text: Directory Connector is one Windows instance per Active Directory domain. SCIM 2.0 is a REST sync with no on-premises connector. Org SSO maps uid . Partner SSO maps mail . A dry run comes before the first full sync, and invite suppression requires SSO.

steps.title: Takeaway 1
steps.text: One Directory Connector instance serves one Active Directory domain. Download it from Control Hub. A trial or any paid subscription is required to reach the software. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 2
steps.text: The only required cloud attribute is uid . Cisco recommends mail or userPrincipalName , and the chosen attribute must be in email format. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 3
steps.text: Do a dry run before the first full synchronization. Incremental sync stays disabled until a full sync has completed. Group synchronization requires a full sync. [cite:1]

steps.title: Three provisioning paths, one uid
steps.text: Control Hub is where you view users, assign licenses, download Directory Connector, and configure SSO when you want users to authenticate through an identity provider and you do not want to send Webex App email invitations. [cite:1] Directory synchronization is shown as disabled until you install the connector and a full synchronization succeeds. [cite:1]

steps.title: One thing that breaks
steps.text: Control Hub still shows directory synchronization disabled — Finish install, dry run, then full sync.

steps.title: What this room is
steps.text: Automatic assignments grant Calling, Meetings, Messaging, and Contact Center when a person is added. A license typed onto a new user at creation skips that template. Webex spends the oldest subscription first. Calling still needs a location and an extension or number. A professional workspace license does not downgrade to common area.

steps.title: Takeaway 1
steps.text: Organization and group templates combine. If one template adds a license and another removes the same license, the user still receives it. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 2
steps.text: Existing users is checked only for the save you are making. The next visit shows it unselected. Preserve licenses for existing users is selected for you when you choose Existing users. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 3
steps.text: Nested groups do not inherit the parent group’s license assignment. The groups hierarchy in Control Hub is flat. A user’s effective licenses are still the combination of every group assignment they belong to, including the parent, when those assignments are applied to them. [cite:1]

steps.title: Templates, then the Calling exception
steps.text: Automatic licensing grants Webex licenses to new users without a manual assignment for each person. The organization path is Management, Users, Licenses. The group path is Management, Groups, the group, Assignments. [cite:1] Webex does not support auto-assignment to Active Directory distribution groups. Synchronize groups that use a Group Policy. [cite:1]

steps.title: One thing that breaks
steps.text: Template licenses never land on a new API or CSV user — Create without a specific license if the organization template should apply.

steps.title: What this room is
steps.text: A location is a physical address that can hold both calling and workspaces. A user belongs to one location. A workspace belongs to one location. Webex generates a Location ID. Changing the location time zone does not change the time zone already stored on an auto attendant, hunt group, or call queue.

steps.title: Takeaway 1
steps.text: Create a location at Management > Locations > Manage location > Create manually. Name, country or region, and street address are required. Webex generates a Location ID. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 2
steps.text: A user can be assigned to only one location. A workspace can be assigned to only one location. Manual add from the location is up to 25 users. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 3
steps.text: A location with Webex Calling cannot be deleted until you click Disable calling. Calling users or workspaces on it cannot be removed from the location until the Webex Calling license is removed. [cite:1]

steps.title: The address is the anchor
steps.text: Locations organize users and workspaces by a physical location identified by an address. The same location can carry calling and workspace management. The article’s header on the retrieved page is June 05, 2026. [cite:1]

steps.title: What this room is
steps.text: Three different clocks live in Control Hub: 21 days of call troubleshooting, 3 or 13 months of analytics, and 30 days of uploaded client logs. Mixing them up is how a ticket goes looking in the wrong room.

steps.title: Takeaway 1

steps.title: Takeaway 2

steps.title: What this room is
steps.text: The country you select while provisioning permanently sets the GEO for the organization’s users and encryption keys. Webex does not currently support migrating between GEO locations. Meetings follow the site time zone. Calling follows the principal place of business given at order time. You read the result at Account > Info > Data Locations.

steps.title: Takeaway 1
steps.text: Identities, encryption keys, and encrypted user-generated content are stored in the organization’s geographic region. The Key Management Service in that region handles key requests for spaces, messages, and content in Webex App. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 2

steps.title: Takeaway 3

steps.text: The introduction to migrating Unified CM to Webex Calling is dated January 14, 2026. It points at the Cisco Preferred Architecture for Webex Calling for the fuller design. This room quotes the guide’s component list and the before-and-after tables. It does not invent Preferred Architecture diagrams. [cite:1]

steps.title: What this room is
steps.text: Every location picks one PSTN path. Local Gateway is the premises session border controller that keeps your carrier. It is not the registrar for phones.

steps.title: Takeaway 1
steps.text: Webex Calling documents three PSTN choices, selected per location: Cisco PSTN (Cisco Calling Plan), Cloud Connected PSTN, and premises-based PSTN (Local Gateway). You may mix them across locations. Each location has one. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 2
steps.text: Local Gateway terminates a trunk on a supported session border controller. Two trunk models exist: registration-based and certificate-based. They differ in scale and device support. [cite:2] [cite:3]

steps.title: Takeaway 3
steps.text: Registration-based trunks are up to 250 concurrent calls per trunk and support only CUBE. Certificate-based trunks are for more than 250 concurrent calls per trunk and a choice of device types. [cite:3]

steps.title: Choose the path before you touch dial peers
steps.text: The calling setup article is blunt: the PSTN choice is at location level, each location has only one PSTN option, and you can mix options across a deployment. After you provision an option you can change it from Manage on the location’s PSTN properties, but some options — Cisco PSTN is the example — may not be available once another option was assigned. Open a support case for guidance rather than clicking until it…

steps.title: One thing that breaks
steps.text: Trunk never registers — Re-copy credentials from Control Hub. Do not keep typing a password from a screenshot in a guide.

steps.title: What this room is
steps.text: Internal dialing is an organization length plus a per-location prefix. Enterprise dial plans are global, one routing choice, and a pattern language with two wildcards that are illegal in the middle. PSTN is chosen per location: Cisco Calling Plan, Cloud Connected PSTN, or premises-based PSTN through a local gateway. Cloud PSTN serves Webex Calling users. Calls that start on the premises do not use it.

steps.title: Takeaway 1
steps.text: Internal extension length is 2–10 digits, default 4. Routing prefix length is 1–7 and includes the steering digit, so a length of 4 leaves 3 digits for the site. Lengthening extensions does not rewrite speed dials. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 2
steps.text: If extensions repeat across locations, turn off extension dialing between locations. The caller then dials the Enterprise Significant Number: routing prefix plus extension. Directory Connector must not already contain the prefix, or Webex adds it again. User extensions should not start with the steering digit or the outbound dial digit. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 3
steps.text: An enterprise dial plan is global for all users and has one routing choice, a trunk or a route group. Patterns are ESN/on-net, +E.164, or a SIP URI domain. X is one digit. ! is only at the end of an E.164 pattern, once. 617495X3XX and 1617495X3! are illegal. [cite:2]

steps.title: Three PSTN choices, one pattern language
steps.text: After a location exists, PSTN is assigned there: Cisco PSTN, Cloud Connected PSTN, or premises-based PSTN. The path in the trunk article is Calling > Locations, then Assign or Manage. Cloud PSTN does not carry calls that originate from premises users. [cite:2]

A subscription cap, and webhooks for…

steps.title: Takeaway 1
steps.text: Connect’s own page lists six areas: channel provisioning, integration setup, flow orchestration, multichannel messaging, NLP/NLU/AI, and enterprise control. Channels include SMS, RCS, Branded Text, WhatsApp, Push, Live Chat and In-App, Email, Voice, MMS, Apple Messages for Business, and Messenger. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 2
steps.text: Assets are created in the Connect portal, in Control Hub for Email and Chat, or through Developer Portal APIs for those digital assets. A service holds the assets, integrations, credentials, flows, and rules. Flow Builder is the multi-step designer. Rules are the shorter trigger-condition-action path. [cite:1]

steps.title: Takeaway 3
steps.text: Inbound webhooks notify Connect about an external event and can start a flow or a rule. Outbound webhooks deliver receipts and incoming messages. Custom nodes wrap REST or SOAP. Authorizations are a service key or a JWT. [cite:1]

steps.title: Name the editor before you name the API
steps.text: Webex Contact Center Flow Designer is T8-R01. Webex Connect Flow Builder designs multi-step customer flows inside a service. An ICM script is the Enterprise editor, and T6-R04 keeps that import marked. Connect’s page also has Rules, which are triggers, conditions, and actions for shorter work. [cite:1]
